slides.title: The revision connects the planned cycle to a controlled update case
slides.notes:
The original plan was to demonstrate a change in conditions, detect consequential degradation, justify and prepare an update, retain historical performance, calibrate uncertainty, and independently review deployment. The updated report now maps an existing controlled U-Net study onto that plan. MONITOR has baseline aggregates; DETECT is a retrospective response label; DECIDE uses an illustrative screen; PREPARE is regime-selected; UPDATE has the strongest reported evidence. None of those labels establishes operational monitoring or an approved decision record. CALIBRATE and DEPLOY remain requirements. This is the report revision contribution, not a claim of new experiments.

Source: Revised report §§2.2, 5.9.

slides.title: The case study tests adaptation to rare plume changes
slides.notes:
The reported case is a pump-and-treat U-Net on a 128 × 100 grid with 1–5 extraction wells and a dataset described as 10,000 physics simulations. Pumping input is represented through Thiem preprocessing. Time is kept indexed because older descriptions disagree on days versus years. Historical cases are the bottom 40% of the Mass90 size-change response score, with cutoff 0.133; rare cases are the top 3%, starting at 0.329. This score requires the reference next state and is not a prospective warning signal. It can miss plume translation that leaves the footprint size unchanged. Rare cases and historical replay define the update problem; trajectory splits, middle-57% handling, controller exposure, and active-learning selection are not verified.

Source: Revised report §§5.1–5.5; manuscript Fig. 1.

slides.title: The rare-case example locates the baseline prediction error
slides.notes:
This is a faithful crop of the original manuscript rare-regime triplet. The caption identifies the reference as the full-order physics field and the prediction as the static U-Net result. All pixels, original labels, axes, aspect ratio, and colorbars are preserved; this is not a numerical replot. Concentration ranges to 813.6 µg/L and signed error spans ±169.4 µg/L in the displayed source. The field shows localized residual structure around the plume. No sample identifier or raw arrays accompany it, so this is illustrative of the physical error mechanism and not an independently verified distributional result. Historical and rare source panels use different scales; only the internally consistent rare triplet is shown. No synthetic plume or recolored pixel-derived field has been created.

Source: Manuscript Fig. 2(b), rare-regime triplet; source crop.

slides.title: Rare-regime recovery comes with a historical-retention tradeoff
slides.notes:
Compare both objectives: baseline 0.58/10.04, simple fine-tuning 1.11/3.92, fixed replay 1.03/1.21, and EWC 5.45/1.22 µg/L. Fixed replay has lower errors than simple fine-tuning or EWC in this particular comparison, while remaining worse than the baseline on historical conditions. It reduces rare RMSE by 87.9% and raises historical RMSE by 77.6%. Supporting rare-plume metrics change from 32.30 to 1.82% for mass, 14.20 to 3.43% for peak, and 7.11 to 1.89% for Mass90. Exact normalization requires code. The ambiguous historical plume-metric column is omitted. No line between points is drawn because training trajectories are unavailable. The Figure 3 full-network 0.64/0.99 pair is not pooled here because Model C and protocols remain unresolved.

Source: Manuscript Fig. 4; revised report Table 10.

slides.title: An explicit screen retains two controller outcomes for further evaluation
slides.notes:
This is a separate Figure 5 controller comparison. Fixed replay is 80.4/88.9%, threshold adaptive forgetting 26.5/85.8%, loss-balanced 21.1/85.5%, and loss-balanced with floor 38.1/87.3%, where coordinates are historical increase and rare reduction. The shaded region meets historical increase ≤30% and rare reduction ≥85%. The two passing variants are candidates under this illustrative screen, not approved deployments. Historical margins are 3.5 and 8.9 points; rare margins are 0.8 and 0.5 points. Replicate uncertainty is absent, so significance or robustness cannot be inferred. Figure 4 fixed-replay changes 77.6/87.9 differ from Figure 5 80.4/88.9; keep those comparisons separate until denominators, splits, and executed configurations are reconciled.

Source: Manuscript Fig. 5; revised report Table 9.

slides.title: The evidence stops before calibration and final validation
slides.notes:
The report reaches a defensible result: retain two controller outcomes for further evaluation, then hold for missing evidence. There are no predictive intervals, calibrated coverage/width results, independent calibration parameters, untouched final-test record, checkpoint identity, or versioned promotion decision for these outcomes. The figure labels required roles rather than claiming verified independent partitions. A deterministic model could use residual-based conformal calibration when suitable data and assumptions exist; coverage is not inferred from RMSE. This is an offline evidence assessment, not an operational rollback event. If an operational incumbent becomes invalid, withdrawal and governed retraining policy applies.

Source: Revised report §§5.7–5.9.

slides.title: The next demonstration must connect a known change to a validated update
slides.notes:
Return to the original demonstration purpose. First resolve the time axis and trajectory manifest and archive executed configurations and predictions. Define a known controlled change, evaluate the detector prospectively on ordered trajectories, and freeze thresholds and an acceptance contract before final testing. Compare adaptive scheduling with fixed replay at r = 0.8 under matched seeds, update budget, and historical/new exposure; the displayed adaptive trajectory reaches that cap, which alone cannot isolate scheduling benefit. Calibrate independently and evaluate an untouched final test once, then record model version and reviewer decision. The diagram is an experiment plan, not an achieved result. Field deployment and long-duration monitoring remain subsequent validation, and no cost/speedup or active-learning gain is claimed.

Source: Revised report §5.10; analysis specification; original trigger/UQ plan.
